blind_target.authors: Kozel, F. A.; Revell, L. J.; Lorberbaum, J. P.; Shastri, A.; Elhai, J. D.; Horner, M. D.; Smith, A.; Nahas, Z.; Bohning, D. E.; George, M. S.
blind_target.title: A pilot study of functional magnetic resonance imaging brain correlates of deception in healthy young men.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
The Lie-minus-True group map revealed significant
activation in similar regions from the prior cohorts using this
paradigm (see Figure and Table). Specifically, the regions of
right orbitofrontal, right inferior frontal, right middle frontal,
and right cingulate gyrus have replicated now in five
independent groups from four studies across several
paradigms [3-5].
blind_target.outcome_quote:
This method for detecting deception was successfully
replicated on a different scanner at a different location for
both the individual and group analyses.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The explicit overall verdict states successful replication for both group and individual analyses. It covers the group-level findings attributed to references 3–5, outweighing the specific left temporal contrast.
